Travel Documents

Traveling abroad while your immigration process is pending requires special authorization. Our immigration team in Florida helps you obtain or renew your travel documents quickly and safely, ensuring full compliance with USCIS rules.

Whether you live in Miami or Orlando, our experts guide you through the advance parole process, preparing all forms and evidence needed for smooth approval. We protect your right to travel without risking your immigration status.

From Tampa to Fort Lauderdale, our immigration professionals assist individuals and families across Florida in securing travel permits efficiently and correctly.

What is the travel document service?

A travel document, often called advance parole, allows certain noncitizens to travel abroad and reenter the U.S. legally while their immigration cases are pending. It’s essential for applicants awaiting adjustment of status or asylum decisions.

Our immigration office prepares and submits Form I-131, ensuring all documentation meets USCIS standards. We also track your case until the travel document is approved and delivered safely.

This service helps you plan international trips confidently, without losing the progress or validity of your ongoing immigration process.

What benefits do you receive by hiring this service?

Choosing our immigration team in Florida for travel document assistance provides clarity, accuracy, and peace of mind from start to finish.

  • Expert preparation of Form I-131
  • Eligibility verification and risk assessment
  • Fast and complete application submission
  • Secure guidance for urgent or family-related travel
  • Tracking and updates until approval
  • Bilingual communication in English and Spanish
  • Support for renewals and reapplications

With professional help, you can travel abroad safely while maintaining full compliance with immigration laws.

How does the travel document process work?

Understanding how the advance parole process works helps you plan correctly and prevent delays or travel complications.

  1. Determine eligibility for advance parole or reentry permit
  2. Prepare supporting documents and travel justification
  3. Complete and file Form I-131 with USCIS
  4. Pay the filing fee and receive your receipt notice
  5. Attend biometrics appointment if required
  6. Receive your approved travel document by mail

Our specialists handle each step carefully, ensuring you travel legally and reenter the U.S. without issues.

What should you know before applying for a travel document?

Before applying, make sure your immigration case allows travel authorization. Leaving the U.S. without it may cancel your pending application.

Gather all required documents, such as ID, pending case receipts, and proof of emergency or travel purpose. Our team ensures everything is filed correctly to avoid rejection.

Being well-prepared helps you travel safely, comply with regulations, and protect your U.S. immigration status.

FAQ

Here are the most common questions about travel documents in Florida, answered clearly to help you plan your trip securely.

Who can apply for a travel document?

Applicants with pending adjustment of status, DACA, or asylum cases may apply for advance parole to travel temporarily abroad.

How long does it take to get a travel document?

Processing times vary from 3 to 6 months, depending on USCIS workload and your case urgency.

Can I travel without a travel document?

No, leaving the U.S. without advance parole may result in the automatic cancellation of your pending immigration case.

Is the travel document valid for multiple trips?

It depends on the approval. Some documents allow multiple entries within the validity period, usually one year.

Can I renew my travel document?

Yes, you can renew it before expiration if your immigration process is still pending or ongoing.

Do I need to attend a biometrics appointment?

In some cases, yes. USCIS may require fingerprints or photos before issuing the travel document.

Can I work with a travel document?

No, the travel document only authorizes international travel and reentry. You’ll need a valid EAD for work permission.

Is hiring professional help necessary?

Yes, professional assistance ensures your application is complete, accurate, and submitted under the correct category.

If your question wasn’t answered, contact our immigration team today for personalized assistance with your travel documents in Florida.
